headline: Australian data-centre operator CDC and the AI company Firmus have called off their plan to build up to 1.6 gigawatts of AI data centres together, after only 42 megawatts were delivered.
score_reason: Kept at the pool score of 6: a large announced AI build-out is called off shortly before a major share listing, and the two sides frame it differently.
importance_line: What changed is that the plan to build AI data centres across Australia, which Firmus said could involve up to A$73.3 billion and had projected would create up to 20,700 direct jobs by 2028, has been called off ahead of Firmus's planned 23 Oct 2026 share listing, which matters to the Australian workers and regions it was meant to serve, then to investors weighing the share offer, then to Firmus and CDC, and the doubt is that the two sides frame the split differently and it is not known what will replace the plan.
summary: Rampart reports, as relayed by Startup Daily, that CDC and Firmus are ending Project Southgate, a partnership announced in October 2025 to build up to 1.6 gigawatts of AI computing capacity across Australia by 2028 that delivered only 42 megawatts, in Melbourne, and that CDC's founder Greg Boorer said his company is unlikely to build more data centres for Firmus. It follows our 3 Oct 2026 edition, which carried a Reuters report that investors were divided over Firmus's valuation ahead of its planned Australian share listing on 23 Oct 2026; new today is that Firmus chief executive Oliver Curtis told Startup Daily the two companies “mutually agreed earlier this year” not to proceed, a decision he said does not affect Firmus's current plans or contracted customer capacity.
notes: Pool item is Startup Daily, which credits Rampart as the first reporter, so Rampart is the source and its link is used (Rampart's article is for subscribers; its opening and the Startup Daily and W.Media texts were read). The AFR also reported it. Follow-up of the 3 Oct 2026 Firmus item (pool 1003:C07-10). The '$73.3 billion' in the Startup Daily headline is Australian dollars (W.Media: up to AU$73.3bn).
